stage1.impression: A copper-looking hammered bowl of printed, opaque coins sits on a pale, pinkish timber stand against a dark, blotchy stone wall, with a flat milky-grey block filling the right third. The bowl has some convincing warmth and the depth of field helps, but the salmon-pink timber with its smooth procedural grain, the blown inside of the bowl, the black tab pushed under the rim, and the featureless grey panel all read as a render, not a photograph. As it stands this is a generic still life, not a specific place: you cannot see the door, the shopfront or anything that says Planet EARF, and a magazine would not run it.

blocking_9: The shopfront and door beyond must read as a night street through glass (dark street, a street lamp's glow, the etched name), not a flat grey block: region [940,350,1200,680] lum_median <= 70 with lum_range >= 120
The brightest large surface in the frame must be the bowl and its coins, not the stand top: stand [200,660,845,800] lum_median <= 85, while the bowl keeps lum_median >= 75
The bowl must read as brass, not copper or rose gold: delta_e to #B08D57 <= 10 on [400,690,700,730]
No blown highlight inside the bowl: clip_pct <= 1.0 on [440,600,690,640]
The stand must read as real oiled oak or fir, with open grain and a mitred or jointed edge, not a pink, smooth procedural slab
The wall must read as board-formed concrete (board grain, pour lines, tie holes) at 1:1, not smudged stone tiles
The bowl must look full (about 40 coins, as the card says), heaped, with coins catching small edge highlights the way cast acrylic does
The black object under the bowl's rim must sit on the stand as a believable prop (a matchbook) and not pass under the bowl

defects.what: Inside of the bowl blown: 13.8 % clipped, so the hammered texture is lost in a white hot spot
Stand top is the brightest large area (lum_median 125.5) and salmon pink (RGB median 182/113/79); its grain is smooth, procedural wave bands with no pores; the edge is a plain soft box
Light on the stand rises toward the right edge (profile 44 to 192) instead of pooling on the bowl, so the key looks like it comes from off the stand, not from a downlight above the bowl
Flat black notched plate (presumably a matchbook) runs under the bowl's rim, so it reads as intersecting the bowl, not resting beside it; it has no thickness, printing or striker
The door and shopfront beyond read as a milky grey block (lum_median 151, low texture), with no street, glass reflections or frame detail; it pulls the eye away from the bowl
The upper right is a flat grey wash (lum_range 16) with two out-of-focus dots; it does not read as a night street or as a glass reflection
The concrete reads as smudged stone panels with blotchy bright patches (e.g. around 330-450, 150-420); no board-form grain, pour lines or tie holes; the panel joints look like tiles
The bowl reads as copper or rose gold, not brass (delta_e 20.9 to #B08D57; RGB 162/87/49)
Only about seven coins, scattered flat in an otherwise empty bowl (the card says 40); the coins read as opaque printed poker chips with a drawn pattern and dashed rim, not cast acrylic
The composition is about 70 % empty wall, with the subject jammed into the bottom third and the stand cut off by the frame's lower edge
Overall magenta-pink cast across the timber, bowl and wall; it reads as a grade, not as 2400-2700 K tungsten

changes.problem: The key light overexposes the stand top and blows out the inside of the bowl, so the stand outshines the subject and the hammered brass turns to a white hot spot.

evidence.measured: bowl interior clip_pct 13.8, lum_p95 248.8; stand [200,660,845,800] lum_median 125.5, which is brighter than the bowl's 82.5

change.setting: the downlight over the host stand (one of the Domes' downlights, 140.0 W, 20.0 deg) or render exposure
change.from: 140.0 W spot, cone 20 deg, aimed so the pool falls to the stand's right edge; exposure 5.4
change.to: a dedicated narrow spot on the bowl of about 60 W, cone 14 deg, aimed at the bowl's centre so the pool's edge falls just past the bowl onto the stand; or keep the Dome's downlight and lower exposure to 4.9

changes.expected: The bowl becomes the brightest thing, with its hammered facets showing as many small highlights; the stand falls off from the bowl outward.

changes.problem: The door and shopfront beyond read as a flat, milky grey block instead of glass onto a night street.

evidence.measured: lum_median 150.8 with a soft edge (step 5.7, 11 px wide at x 930-960); upper part [940,0,1200,340] lum_range 16.1

change.setting: street lamps (2 x point, 500.0 W, 2700 K) and the window's etched name (0.01)
change.from: street lamps 500 W lighting the glass and reveal evenly; etched name 0.01
change.to: street lamps 150 W, placed outside and beyond the glass so they show as two warm out-of-focus discs; the etched name raised to 0.08 so it reads in reverse on the glass; the inner sill and reveal left dark

changes.expected: The right third goes dark blue-black with two warm bokeh discs and a faint reverse-lettered name, which says 'door, at night' and gives the place a name.

changes.problem: The stand reads as pink, smooth CG wood, not oiled timber.

evidence.measured: RGB median 182/113/79 (salmon); the 1:1 crop shows banded procedural grain with no pores and a soft, featureless edge

change.from: light natural stain, smooth roughness, procedural grain
change.to: a mid-dark oiled oak stain (about #6B4A2E in daylight), roughness 0.45 with variation, an image-based rift-sawn oak texture at true scale (rays visible), and a 2 mm edge radius

changes.expected: The stand reads as a dark, warm oak top that holds the bowl's reflection and shadow without competing with it.

changes.problem: A magenta cast turns the brass to copper and the oak to pink.

evidence.measured: bowl RGB 162/87/49, delta_e 20.9 to brass #B08D57; the wall's G channel sits low against R and B throughout

change.to: +6 toward green (whichever sign removes magenta in this pipeline); keep white_balance_k 3000

changes.expected: Brass reads yellow-gold, oak reads brown, and the concrete reads warm grey rather than mauve.

changes.problem: Two-thirds of the frame is empty wall, the subject sits in the bottom third with the stand cut off, and the door, which is half of the frame's purpose, is not legible.

evidence.measured: a low-information area (lum_range 57) covering about 55 % of the frame; the bowl occupies only rows 580-745

change.to: position about [2.1, 2.6, 1.45] looking down about 15 deg at the bowl, 50 mm, f/2.2, with the bowl on the lower-left third and the door's glass and frame filling the upper right, out of focus

changes.expected: The bowl fills about a third of the frame width, the coins are readable, and the door is a soft but recognisable shape beyond.

changes.problem: The bowl looks nearly empty and the coins lie flat and scattered, which contradicts 'a bowl of 40' and kills the abundance.

evidence.measured: about 7 coins visible over a mostly empty, clipped brass floor

change.setting: props: EARFcoins in the brass bowl at the door
change.to: 40 coins heaped with physics settling so they overlap and tilt, with a few on edge against the wall of the bowl and one or two on the stand beside it

changes.expected: A heaped bowl of tinted coins, with the eight tints scattered through it and edge highlights on the tilted coins.

changes.problem: The black prop under the bowl's rim reads as a flat plate passing under the bowl.

evidence.measured: a notched black slab with no thickness or print, its end hidden under the bowl's rim

change.from: one matchbook pushed under the bowl's rim
change.to: two matchbooks lying fully clear of the bowl, about 40 mm off its foot, one slightly fanned open, with a printed cover (light ink on black card), a striker strip and 3 mm card thickness

changes.expected: A clear sign of life beside the bowl, with no intersection.

changes.problem: The wall reads as smudged stone tiles, not board-formed concrete.

evidence.measured: lum_range 38; the 1:1 crop shows soft blotches with no board grain, pour lines or tie holes; the joints read as tile joints

change.setting: the concrete's tone and sheen (materials' finish)
change.to: a board-formed albedo and bump at true scale (boards about 150 mm, horizontal fir grain imprint, 25 mm tie-hole cones at 600 x 900 centres, faint pour lines), roughness 0.8 with a slight sheen variation

changes.expected: At 1:1 the wall reads as poured concrete with wood-grain imprint and catches the spill from the bowl's light as grain texture.

out_of_scope.request: Make the coins read as cast acrylic (translucent tint, polished glowing edges, the globe engraved, not printed) rather than opaque printed poker chips
out_of_scope.why: The coins are an EARF product, so their material and design are fixed. It matters a lot: the coins are the only colour in the frame and now read as casino chips.

out_of_scope.request: Confirm whether the bowl should be hammered or plain spun brass
out_of_scope.why: The card says brass but not what finish, and the bowl is part of the host stand's set design, which the card fixes.
